title: Field iso-surface: marching tetrahedra leaves slivers that collapse at the 1e-9 weld when a cut floor lies on the sample lattice

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
### What happened

`iso::extract_with(f, step, IsoMethod::Marching)` (`iso.rs`, `tet`) puts a mesh corner a few picometres from a sample when a field value at that sample is almost zero. This happens when a cut floor lies on the sample lattice (the field's cell centres). The facets that share that sample then have two corners less than 1e-9 mm apart. They are not exactly zero-area, so `push` keeps them. After the 1e-9 weld that `open_edges` uses (and after an f32 export), they collapse, and the edges next to them are on three or more facets. The mesh is then not a valid solid.

`open_edges` counts only edges with an odd number of facets. An edge on four facets passes, so the existing closed-mesh tests do not see this.

Dual contouring (the default) is not affected in the same steps. Marching tetrahedra is reached by name and as the fallback when a dual mesh is not closed (`extract_with`).

Measured on main f8748d97d with a synthetic block (steps below):

| Floor height | Method | Facets | Collapsed after the 1e-9 weld | Edges on 3+ facets | Odd edges |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 15.25 (on the lattice) | Dual | 305,928 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 15.25 (on the lattice) | Marching | 1,216,284 | 11,394 | 5799 | 0 |
| 15.1 (off the lattice) | Dual | 306,320 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 15.1 (off the lattice) | Marching | 1,217,748 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

The field distance at the lattice sample over the floor at 15.25 is -1e-12. At 15.1 it is 0.15.

We found it in our own lane, which meshes field stock with marching tetrahedra at cell 0.254 mm. Every collapsed facet that we located had its shared corner on a lattice sample, at cut-floor heights, and none were on the mesh's clip box.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `Stock::block(Backend::Field { band: FIELD_BAND }, 0.0, 0.0, 30.0, 30.0, 20.0, 0.5)`. The lattice samples are at (k + 0.5) * 0.5, so 15.25 is one.
2. `simulate` four feed moves of a flat tool of radius 3 at z 15.25: from (4, y) to (26, y) for y = 8, 12, 16, 20.
3. `iso::extract_with(field, field.cell(), IsoMethod::Marching)`.
4. Weld the corners on the 1e-9 lattice (as `open_edges` does). Count the facets with two equal corners and the edges with more than two facets.

Expected: 0 and 0, as for the dual mesh and for the floor at 15.1.

### Proposed fix

In `tet`'s `cross`, snap the crossing to the sample when it is within a small fraction of the edge from it (for example, `t` below 1e-6 or above 1 - 1e-6). The coincident corner is then exact, and `push` already drops the zero-area sliver. Also let the closed-mesh check (or a sibling of `open_edges`) count edges on more than two facets, so that tests see this class.

Pin: the steps above give 0 collapsed facets and 0 edges on 3+ facets for `IsoMethod::Marching`, and the mesh stays closed (0 odd edges) with the same volume as before. We have not yet tested the proposed snap.

### Version and OS

main f8748d97d (source build), Windows 11.

### Labels

We cannot set labels. Our suggestion: `bug`, `area:sim`, `P3`.
